blockers.quote: You feel nothing. But a night you sell is a night your own brain doesn't get.
blockers.why: Check #3, Second hook by 0:30: the draft's timing note places this loss at about 0:55, so the opening shows the reward without establishing what is at risk by 0:30.
blockers.fix: Move the cost directly after line 34: "You get paid for every hour. But every hour you sell is a night your own brain doesn't get." Remove line 65 afterward.

blockers.quote: The band came with a leaflet. It sets out the deal.
blockers.why: Check #16, A flagged limit that pays off: the rule runs across seven spoken lines and never explicitly flags the crumbs for recall.
blockers.fix: Compress lines 86-100 to three rule lines: "The leaflet says: wear the band to bed, and while you sleep the company rents your brain and pays by the hour." / "One company can link many bands, for one big job. But the leaflet promises each brain stays separate. One brain, one band, one jar." / "You remember none of the work—only crumbs: a taste, a word, a face that isn't yours. It calls them harmless. Remember that."

blockers.quote: So what's the job? The crumbs fit together. Into a drawing. And the drawing is a machine.
blockers.why: Check #18, A running gag that carries the peak: the globe and machine reveal are the named peak, but the four-time "What'd you get?" gag does not participate in it.
blockers.fix: Immediately before this line, insert: "Brother: What'd we get?" Then let the drawing becoming a machine answer him.

suggestions.quote: Therefore sleeping for money is a day job. So the couple across the street sleep in shifts, and their jar never stops. And the empty warehouse by the bridge fills with cots, and a clerk with a clipboard stands at its door.
suggestions.fix: Replace the announced connectors with the causal turn: "The nap room proves sleep can be sold twice: once to the company, once to the boss. Across the street, a couple starts sleeping in shifts, and their jar never stops. By the bridge, an empty warehouse starts filling with cots."

suggestions.quote: Morning four. You fold a fitted sheet into a perfect square. Nobody can fold a fitted sheet. His spoon hits the floor.
suggestions.fix: Beat the familiar fitted-sheet gag with a backfire: "Morning four. You fold a fitted sheet into a perfect square. Then one wrong corner ties the whole bed into a knot. His spoon hits the floor."

suggestions.quote: You remember nothing of your nights. Only the crumbs. And now you know what they were building. You'd rather sit in that chair every Thursday than build it every night.
suggestions.fix: Let the drawer reveal the decision instead of announcing it: "You remember nothing of your nights. Only the crumbs. At eleven fifty-eight, the contract finally costs more than the chair."

keep.quote: It makes the evening news. Nobody's up to watch it.
Brother: Fine. I'll fail something. You can come to the retake.
